title: 6.7.23 Two-Player Pong-Sumo
description: Graded: build a two-player Pong-Sumo game: two paddles, one ball, push the ball past the opponent to score. Incorporates two-player input, push-collision physics, a win condition, and at least one joint. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Arena setup: canvas and gravity
steps.instructions: Create a canvas (e.g. 600×400). Set world.gravity.y = 0 so paddles and ball glide instead of falling.
hints: Check the Canvas section of the moSHion docs drawer. For no-gravity setup see 2.7.25.

steps.title: Top and bottom walls
steps.instructions: Add two static sprites along the top and bottom edges as walls so the ball can't escape vertically.
hints: Check the Sprite section of the moSHion docs drawer. Set collider = 'static' on each wall.

steps.title: Two paddles: Player 1 (WASD) and Player 2 (arrow keys)
steps.instructions: Create two paddle sprites (one on the left, one on the right). In draw(), read kb.pressing for W/S (Player 1) and up/down (Player 2) and set each paddle's velocity accordingly.
hints: See 2.7.25 for the two-paddle pattern. Check kb.pressing in the moSHion docs drawer.

steps.title: Ball: bouncy, dynamic, initial velocity
steps.instructions: Create a ball sprite in the center. Set a positive bounciness so it bounces off paddles and walls. Give it an initial vel.x so the game starts moving.
hints: See 2.7.24 (bounciness) and 2.7.25 (two paddles) for the arena setup pattern.

steps.title: Add at least one joint
steps.instructions: Use a DistanceJoint or HingeJoint somewhere in your game: a boundary chain, a moving obstacle, or an attachment between two sprites. Use new DistanceJoint(a, b) and set joint.length = N after construction if you want a specific length.
hints: See 2.7.12 (DistanceJoint) or 2.7.14 (HingeJoint). Remember: joint.delete() releases the constraint. Set length with joint.length = N after new DistanceJoint(a, b).

steps.title: Score variables and initial state
steps.instructions: Declare p1Score and p2Score at the top (outside setup/draw). Initialize both to 0 in setup(). Set gameState to 'title' so the game starts on the title screen.
hints: The moSHion docs drawer has sprite position properties. Compare ball.pos.x against 0 and the canvas width.

steps.title: State-machine draw(): title, play, win
steps.instructions: Wrap your draw() logic in a switch(gameState) with cases for 'title', 'play', and 'win'. In 'play': move paddles with kb.pressing, check ball edge zones to score, render scores with text(), check the win threshold. In 'win': show the winner and wire a key to reset.
hints: See 2.6.1 (state machine pattern) for switch(state) with cases and break.

requirements.title: Two-player keyboard input
requirements.description: Both players have keys assigned: kb.pressing is called with at least two different keys (one per player).

requirements.title: Independent per-player score variables
requirements.description: p1Score and p2Score (or equivalent) are declared at module scope: one for each player.

requirements.title: Push-collision physics tuned with bounciness
requirements.description: At least one sprite has its bounciness set (e.g. ball.bounciness = 0.9).

requirements.title: Top-down arena: no gravity
requirements.description: world.gravity.y is set to 0 so the sprites glide instead of falling.

requirements.title: Live score rendered with text()
requirements.description: draw() calls text(...) with p1Score or p2Score so the current score is visible on screen.

requirements.title: Win condition fires on a threshold
requirements.description: A comparison against a winning number (e.g. p1Score >= 5) triggers the win condition.

requirements.title: At least one joint is used
requirements.description: A DistanceJoint or HingeJoint is created somewhere in the game (boundary, obstacle, or attachment).
